chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) permitted the women and the weak to depart from Jam' at night and to throw the Jamarah at night. So if they wish to visit the House, they should appoint someone to slaughter on their behalf.

key_terms.الضُّعَفَاءِ: The weak (those excused from full exertion)
key_terms.الْجَمْرَةَ: The Jamarah (the stone pillars in Mina)
key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Muzdalifa (the place where pilgrims gather after Mina)

ai.seo_question: What are the Hajj concessions for women and the weak regarding departure from Muzdalifa and slaughtering sacrifices?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic principle of *rukhas* (concessions) in Hajj jurisprudence, specifically alleviating the burden of night-long standing at Muzdalifa for women, children, and the weak. It underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the timing of the Jamarah stoning and the delegation of sacrificial duties, reflecting the practical ease (*taysir*) intended by the Sharia for those with physical limitations.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, and someone else, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww permitted for the women and the children that they depart from Jam’a at night, and that they should pelt the Jamarah at night. So if they intend that they visit the House (Kabah), they should appoint someone who would slaughter on their behalf’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy and others from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, permitted women and the weak ones to leave from Jam‘ during the night. They were allowed to throw pebbles during the night and visit the House, if they wanted to do so, and they were allowed to appoint someone to slaughter offering on their behalf.’”
